questions.text: Rearrange the following four sentences (A), (B), (C), and (D) in the proper sequence to form a meaningful paragraph. A. The policy, however, failed to account for the informal sector which employs a vast majority of the workforce. B. In 2020, the government unveiled a comprehensive labour code consolidating twenty-nine central laws. C. Consequently, a significant portion of workers remained outside the ambit of social security benefits. D. The new code aimed to simplify compliance and ensure uniform wage protection across industries.
questions.solution: Shortcut: Identify the opening sentence (B introduces the topic with a specific time/event). Link 'However' in A to the positive aim in D. 'Consequently' in C follows the failure mentioned in A. Sequence: B-D-A-C. Full Solution: Sentence B is the clear opener introducing the 2020 Labour Code. Sentence D elaborates on the code's aims. Sentence A contrasts this aim using 'however', pointing out the failure regarding the informal sector. Sentence C provides the result ('Consequently') of that failure. Only option BDAC maintains this logical flow.

questions.text: Read the following sentence to find out whether there is any grammatical error in it. The error, if any, will be in one part of the sentence. Select the part with the error. If the sentence is free from error, select 'No error'. The manager insisted on (A) / the employees to work (B) / overtime to meet (C) / the project deadline. (D)
questions.solution: Shortcut: Spot the main verb 'insisted on' — it mandatorily takes a Gerund (verb+ing) or a 'that-clause', never an infinitive (to+verb). Scan Option B for 'to work'; it violates this pattern instantly. Step-by-step: (1) Segment: A='The manager insisted on', B='the employees to work', C='overtime to meet', D='the project deadline'. (2) Check verb pattern: 'Insist on' requires object + gerund (e.g., 'employees working') or 'that' + subjunctive ('that employees work'). (3) Option B uses 'to work' (infinitive), which is grammatically incorrect after 'insisted on'. (4) Options A, C, D are structurally sound. (5) Hence, error lies in Part B.
questions.topic: Error Detection - Verb Patterns (Gerund vs Infinitive)

questions.text: Find the unit digit of the expression (7^95 - 3^58).
questions.solution: Shortcut (Cyclicity): Unit digit of powers of 7 repeats in cycle of 4: 7, 9, 3, 1. 95 ÷ 4 gives remainder 3 → 3rd position in cycle = 3. Unit digit of powers of 3 repeats in cycle of 4: 3, 9, 7, 1. 58 ÷ 4 gives remainder 2 → 2nd position in cycle = 9. Unit digit of (3 - 9) requires borrowing → (13 - 9) = 4. Step-by-step: 7^95 = 7^(4×23+3) → Unit digit same as 7^3 = 343 → 3. 3^58 = 3^(4×14+2) → Unit digit same as 3^2 = 9. Since 3 < 9, we borrow 1 from tens place: 13 - 9 = 4. Unit digit is 4.

questions.text: Find the unit digit of the product (347)^123 × (562)^89.
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use cyclicity of unit digits. Unit digit of 347^123 = Unit digit of 7^123. Cyclicity of 7 is 4 (7, 9, 3, 1). 123 mod 4 = 3 → 3rd position = 3. Unit digit of 562^89 = Unit digit of 2^89. Cyclicity of 2 is 4 (2, 4, 8, 6). 89 mod 4 = 1 → 1st position = 2. Required unit digit = 3 × 2 = 6. Step-by-step: 7^1=7, 7^2=49, 7^3=343 (unit 3), 7^4=2401 (unit 1). 123 = 4×30 + 3 → unit digit 3. 2^1=2, 2^2=4, 2^3=8, 2^4=16 (unit 6). 89 = 4×22 + 1 → unit digit 2. Product unit digit = 3 × 2 = 6.

questions.text: Which of the following phrases should replace the phrase in bold to make the sentence grammatically and contextually correct? The rapid proliferation of digital payment platforms **have not only reduced** the reliance on cash but also enhanced financial inclusion in rural areas.
questions.solution: Shortcut: Identify Subject ('The rapid proliferation' - Singular) -> Verb must be Singular ('has'). Eliminate Option B ('have'). Check Parallelism: 'Not only reduced (V3)... but also enhanced (V3)'. Option A matches perfectly. Full Solution: The subject 'The rapid proliferation' is a singular noun phrase, requiring a singular verb 'has'. Option B uses plural 'have' (SVA error). Option C 'has not only been reducing' (Present Perfect Continuous) breaks parallelism with the simple past participle 'enhanced' following 'but also'. Option A 'has not only reduced' maintains correct Subject-Verb Agreement and parallel structure (Past Participle).

questions.text: A shopkeeper marks his goods 40% above the cost price and allows a discount of 15% on the marked price. Find his gain percent.
questions.solution: Shortcut (Effective Percentage Formula): For successive changes of x% and y%, net % change = x + y + (xy/100). Here, Markup = +40%, Discount = -15%. Net Gain % = 40 + (-15) + (40 × -15)/100 = 25 - 6 = 19%. Step-by-step: Let Cost Price (CP) = Rs. 100. Marked Price (MP) = 100 + 40% of 100 = Rs. 140. Selling Price (SP) after 15% discount = 140 - 15% of 140 = 140 × 0.85 = Rs. 119. Gain = SP - CP = 119 - 100 = Rs. 19. Gain % = (19/100) × 100 = 19%.

questions.text: Read the following information carefully: A @ B means A is the father of B. A # B means A is the mother of B. A $ B means A is the brother of B. A % B means A is the sister of B. How is P related to T in the expression: P @ Q $ R # S % T?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Decode Right-to-Left for generation gaps. T <- S (Sister, same gen) <- R (Mother, +1 gen) <- Q (Brother, same gen) <- P (Father, +1 gen). Total gap from P to T = +2 generations (Male) = Grandfather. Full Solution: P @ Q => P is Father of Q. Q $ R => Q is Brother of R => P is Father of R. R # S => R is Mother of S => P is Maternal Grandfather of S. S % T => S is Sister of T => P is Maternal Grandfather of T.

questions.text: Statements: Some Keys are Locks. All Locks are Doors. No Door is a Window. Conclusions: I. Some Keys are not Windows. II. All Locks being Windows is a possibility. Select the correct option:

options.label: C
options.text: Both Conclusions I and II follow

options.label: D
options.text: Neither Conclusion I nor II follows

questions.solution: Shortcut: Apply standard Venn rules: Some + All = Some; Some + No = Some Not. Possibility is invalid if a definite 'No' relation exists. Full Solution: Some Keys are Locks + All Locks are Doors → Some Keys are Doors. Some Keys are Doors + No Door is Window → Some Keys are not Windows (Conclusion I follows). All Locks are Doors + No Door is Window → No Lock is Window. Since 'No Lock is Window' is definite, the possibility 'All Locks being Windows' cannot exist (Conclusion II does not follow).

questions.text: In what ratio must rice costing Rs. 40 per kg be mixed with rice costing Rs. 55 per kg so that the mixture costs Rs. 48 per kg?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Apply Alligation Rule. Differences: (55 - 48) = 7 and (48 - 40) = 8. Required Ratio (Cheaper : Dearer) = 7 : 8. Step-by-step: Let quantities be x kg and y kg. Equation: (40x + 55y) / (x + y) = 48 => 40x + 55y = 48x + 48y => 7y = 8x => x/y = 7/8.

questions.text: Seven boxes P, Q, R, S, T, U, V are kept one above another in a stack (Bottom position 1, Top position 7). Box V is at the topmost position. There are two boxes between V and P. Box Q is placed immediately below P. There are two boxes between Q and R. Box S is placed above T but below U. Box U is not at the top. Which box is placed at the bottommost position?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Fix definite positions first. 1. V at 7 (Top). 2. Two boxes between V and P => P at 4. 3. Q immediately below P => Q at 3. 4. Two boxes between Q and R => R at 6 (since 3+3=6). 5. Remaining boxes: S, T, U for positions 1, 2, 5. Condition: U > S > T (U above S above T). Only fit: U at 5, S at 2, T at 1. Bottom is T. Full Solution: Pos 7: V. Pos 4: P (gap of 2). Pos 3: Q (below P). Pos 6: R (gap of 2 from Q). Left: 1, 2, 5 for S, T, U. Order U > S > T fits only as U=5, S=2, T=1. Bottom (Pos 1) = T.

questions.text: Fill in the blanks with the most appropriate pair of words. The sudden ______ in global commodity prices ______ a severe strain on the import budget of developing nations.
questions.solution: Shortcut: Subject-Verb Agreement via Head Noun. Identify Subject Head Noun ('surge' - Singular). Eliminate plural verbs ('have') and non-noun subjects ('surging' is participle/gerund, 'surges' is verb). Only 'surge / has' (Singular Noun + Singular Verb) survives. Step-by-step: 1) Locate Subject: 'The sudden surge' (Head noun: 'surge', Singular). 2) Locate Verb: blank 2. 3) Rule: Singular subject takes Singular verb ('has'). 4) Check Option A: 'have' (Plural) -> Out. Option B: 'surges' (Verb form) -> Subject becomes 'The sudden surges' (Plural), verb 'has' (Singular) -> Mismatch. Option D: 'surging' (Gerund/Participle) -> Verb 'have' (Plural) -> Mismatch. Option C: 'surge' (Singular Noun) + 'has' (Singular Verb) -> Correct.

questions.text: Six persons P, Q, R, S, T, and U have different heights. Q is taller than P but shorter than R. S is taller than T but shorter than U. R is shorter than S. P is not the shortest. Who among the following is the tallest?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Chain Formation. Combine statements: 1) R > Q > P. 2) U > S > T. 3) S > R (since R < S). Merge chains: U > S > R > Q > P. Since P is not shortest, T must be shortest. Final Order: U > S > R > Q > P > T. Tallest is U. Full Solution: Write inequalities. R > Q > P. U > S > T. S > R. Combining: U > S > R > Q > P. Only T remains. P > T (since P not shortest). Thus U is tallest.

questions.text: In the following question, a word is given followed by four sentences. Select the sentence in which the usage of the word is INCORRECT or INAPPROPRIATE. Word: **PRECLUDE**

options.label: A
options.text: The new regulations preclude the possibility of early retirement for government servants.

options.label: B
options.text: The heavy downpour precluded the team from playing the final match.

options.label: C
options.text: Her severe allergy to peanuts precludes her to eat at most bakeries.

options.label: D
options.text: The non-disclosure agreement precludes any discussion of the project details.

questions.solution: Shortcut: Memorize the fixed structure **'Preclude + Object + From + Gerund'** or **'Preclude + Noun'**. Eliminate options fitting these; the one using 'Preclude + Object + To + Infinitive' is the answer. Step-by-step: (1) Analyse Option A: 'preclude the possibility' (Preclude + Noun) — Correct. (2) Option B: 'precluded the team from playing' (Preclude + Object + From + Gerund) — Correct. (3) Option C: 'precludes her to eat' uses Infinitive ('to eat') instead of 'from eating' — Incorrect usage. (4) Option D: 'precludes any discussion' (Preclude + Noun) — Correct. (5) Therefore, Option C contains the error.

questions.text: Find the wrong term in the following number series: 2, 3, 6, 15, 45, 156.5, 630
questions.solution: Shortcut: Observe the multiplication pattern: ×1.5, ×2, ×2.5, ×3, ×3.5, ×4. Check each step: 2×1.5=3, 3×2=6, 6×2.5=15, 15×3=45, 45×3.5=157.5 (given 156.5), 157.5×4=630. The term 156.5 breaks the pattern. Full Solution: The series follows a logic where each term is multiplied by an incrementally increasing factor starting from 1.5 with a common difference of 0.5. Calculating sequentially: 2 × 1.5 = 3; 3 × 2 = 6; 6 × 2.5 = 15; 15 × 3 = 45; 45 × 3.5 = 157.5 ≠ 156.5; 157.5 × 4 = 630. Hence, 156.5 is the wrong term.

questions.text: Seven boxes P, Q, R, S, T, U, V are kept one above another (Bottommost position 1, Topmost 7). • Box V is at the bottommost position. • Box R is at an even-numbered position. • There are two boxes between Box R and Box P, with P above R. • Box S is immediately above Box Q. • Box T is immediately below Box U. • Box Q is immediately above Box V. Which box is at the topmost position?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Fix definite positions first. V=1 → Q=2 (above V) → S=3 (above Q). R is even (2,4,6); 2 taken. Two boxes between R and P → P = R+3. If R=4, P=7. If R=6, P=9 (invalid). So R=4, P=7. Remaining slots 5,6 for U,T (U above T) → U=6, T=5. Top (7) = P. Full Solution: 1. V at 1. 2. Q immediately above V → Q at 2. 3. S immediately above Q → S at 3. 4. R at even (4 or 6). Gap of 2 boxes → P at R+3. R=4 → P=7 (valid). R=6 → P=9 (invalid). Thus R=4, P=7. 5. Left slots 5,6. T immediately below U → U=6, T=5. Topmost box (7) is P.
